technical_and_design_decisions: For U1, leverage Spring Data Commons repository abstraction and implement a custom repository using Kafka's changelog topic with off-heap storage via Chronicle Map or MapDB.
For U2 and U3, design a common flush strategy interface that can be configured per module, using acknowledgements from the module-producer to trigger offset and state flushing.
For U4, use the Californium (Cf) CoAP library as the underlying protocol implementation and wrap it as a Spring Integration source adapter.
For U5, create a comprehensive properties file documentation with examples and recommended patterns for deployment manifests.
For U6, integrate with Hadoop's Kerberos authentication mechanism to allow sqoop jobs to run against secured HDFS clusters, using Spring Security for Hadoop if applicable.
For U7, implement a Java client using Spring's RestTemplate or WebClient to interact with the Diego REST API, including proper error handling and authentication.
For U8, refactor the existing ModuleRunner to be Spring Boot-based, leveraging auto-configuration and completing the remaining deployment properties work to eliminate dependency on xd-containers.
assumptions: The developer has prior experience with Spring Framework, Spring Boot, Spring Data, Kafka, CoAP, sqoop, and Cloud Foundry Diego concepts.
Off-heap storage libraries (e.g., Chronicle Map) are available and compatible with Java 17+ as required by Spring Framework 6.0.
The existing codebase is modular and follows Spring patterns, allowing straightforward integration of new features.
Documentation will be written in AsciiDoc or Markdown, integrated into the existing project documentation.
Security for sqoop against HDFS assumes a Kerberized cluster with proper configuration files available.
Diego REST API specifications are stable and publicly documented; authentication uses OAuth2 or basic auth.
The Boot-based ModuleRunner will be built on the latest Spring Boot version compatible with Spring Framework 6.0.
All user stories are independent and can be implemented in parallel where possible, but the developer will work sequentially.

Add support to flush offsets based on successful message acknowledgements from the module-producer. Design flush strategy, implement, test, and document.
Add support to flush state based on successful message acknowledgements from the module-producer. Design flush strategy, implement, test, and document. Likely shares design with offset flush.

Develop a new CoAP source module for consuming data using the Constrained Application Protocol. Includes integration with Californium library, configuration, unit and integration testing, and documentation.

activities.activity_description: Write user documentation explaining how to configure the properties file as a deployment manifest, including recommended settings and examples.

activities.activity_name: Add security support for sqoop jobs against secured HDFS
activities.activity_description: Enable sqoop jobs to run against secured HDFS cluster by integrating Kerberos authentication. Modify configurations, implement security setup, test, and document.

activities.activity_name: Implement Java receptor client for Diego
activities.activity_description: Build a Java client to interact with Diego runtime using the Java receptor REST APIs. Includes REST client implementation, authentication, error handling, tests, and documentation.

activities.activity_name: Implement Boot-based ModuleRunner for container-managed environments
activities.activity_description: Refactor the existing ModuleRunner to be Spring Boot-based, completing remaining deployment properties work to remove reliance on xd-containers. Includes analysis, refactoring, testing, and documentation.

activities.activity_description: Conduct end-to-end integration testing across all implemented user stories, fix any cross-cutting issues, and prepare the release artifacts and notes.
